poti_centre_about.title: About the Centre
poti_centre_about.note: Run by the local seafarers' rights committee together with a port mission. Open daily. Closed 1 Jan, 7 Jan, 26 May.

poti_centre_services.title: Services
poti_centre_services.note: No hot meals cooked — tea, coffee and snacks only.

directions.title: From Checkpoint No.1: ~200 m, 3 min
directions.sub: Cross the road onto Tavdadebuli St. — the club is 200 m ahead on your right, on a lit, paved street

directions.title: From Checkpoint No.2: ~1.1 km, 12–15 min, or 2 min by taxi
From Checkpoint No.3: ~2.5 km — taxi only

poti_transport_leaving.title: Leaving the Port

callout.text: Yes — shore leave is normally permitted at Poti. Always confirm with your Master or ship's agent before you go.

rows.title: No.1 — berths 1–7
rows.sub: Pedestrian

rows.title: No.2 — container berths 8–14
rows.sub: Pedestrian

rows.title: No.3 — container depot
rows.sub: Mostly heavy vehicles

rows.title: Shore Pass
rows.sub: Issued by Border Police through your ship's agent

rows.title: Hi-vis vest and helmet required up to the checkpoint line

poti_transport_leaving.note: All checkpoints operate 24/7. For problems, call your agent or APM security: +995 493 27 77 77.

poti_transport_taxi.title: Taxi

rows.title: Maxim Taxi
rows.sub: The main one here — download it before you arrive

rows.title: Bolt
rows.sub: Works unreliably, especially in the evening

poti_transport_taxi.note: 4–6 GEL (~$1.50–2.20) into the centre. Private drivers without a taxi sticker or app sometimes ask for 20 GEL or $10 for a 2 km ride — use Maxim instead, and expect to pay no more than 5–7 GEL anywhere in Poti.

poti_transport_public.title: Public Transport

rows.title: Marshrutkas 1, 2, 5
rows.sub: To the Central Square and the railway station

poti_transport_public.note: 5–8 minutes to the centre, 0.50–0.80 GEL — cash to the driver (the opposite of Batumi, where cash isn't accepted). Last service around 20:00 — after that, it's taxi only.

poti_currency_exchange.title: Currency Exchange

callout.text: Never exchange money on the street, even for a good rate someone offers you. In some countries this is a criminal offence — and it's one of the most common ways seafarers get scammed near a port.

rows.title: A bank or licensed exchange office
rows.sub: See below — specific business names at the central mall/market are still being confirmed

rows.title: An ATM
rows.sub: Liberty Bank at Checkpoint No.1 — dispenses GEL and USD

rows.title: A stranger offers you a better rate
rows.sub: On the street, at the gate, or "just around the corner" — always a scam

rows.title: No receipt offered
rows.sub: A real exchange always gives you a printed receipt with the rate used

rows.title: Central mall/market, Rustaveli Arch
rows.sub: ~1.1 km · exchange offices operate here alongside the shops

poti_currency_exchange.note: Less confirmed than Batumi's — the ATM at Checkpoint No.1 is the safest bet until specific exchange office names here are checked.

rows.title: Central mall & market — Central Square / Rustaveli Arch
